children: Apple is expected to enter India’s digital payments market with Axis Bank as its first banking partner, while talks with other lenders continue
Apple is set to launch Apple Pay in India next month, beginning with Axis Bank credit cards, marking the company’s entry into one of the world’s largest digital payments markets.

The rollout is expected to start with a single banking partner, with Apple planning to add more lenders through separate agreements. The company has also held discussions with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, although commercial terms with the two lenders have not been finalised.

Apple Pay allows iPhone users to make contactless payments using tokenised card details stored on their devices. Users can authenticate transactions through Face ID, Touch ID, or a device passcode without opening a separate payments app.
Apple Pay To Begin With Card Payments

The initial rollout is expected to focus on credit cards rather than Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions. Apple Pay will allow participating bank customers to add eligible cards to their devices and use them at compatible contactless payment terminals.

Last year, the Reserve Bank of India allowed alternative authentication methods, including biometrics, for card payments. This has enabled services such as Apple Pay to use Face ID and Touch ID for transactions made using Indian bank cards.
Axis Bank is currently the fourth-largest credit card issuer in India. It had around 16.26 million active credit cards in July, according to Reserve Bank of India data.

Apple Pay will enter a digital payments market dominated by UPI, which accounts for about 84 per cent of India’s digital payment volume. UPI supports payments through QR codes, phone numbers, and tap-and-pay features.

Apple’s entry also comes as its presence in India’s smartphone market has expanded. Its market share has doubled to around 8 per cent since 2022, increasing the potential user base for its payments service.

The company plans to expand Apple Pay’s banking partnerships over time, following a phased approach used in other markets. For Indian consumers, the service would provide another option for card-based contactless payments alongside existing digital payment platforms.
